headline: OpenAI delays GPT-5.6 release at US request
summary: OpenAI delays GPT-5.6 release due to US government request
details: The Trump administration has asked OpenAI to delay the release of its GPT-5.6 model. The company will release it in limited preview form, granting access to a small group of enterprise customers.
The government will approve customer access on a case-by-case basis during the preview period. This approach is more favorable than the one given to OpenAI rival Anthropic.
Anthropic was required to suspend access to its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models due to an export control directive. The directive prohibited 'foreign nationals' from accessing the technology.
caption:
Will GPT-5.6 be delayed indefinitely?

The Trump administration has asked OpenAI to delay the release of its GPT-5.6 model. The company will release it in limited preview form, granting access to a small group of enterprise customers.

The government will approve customer access on a case-by-case basis during the preview period. This approach is more favorable than the one given to OpenAI rival Anthropic.

Anthropic was required to suspend access to its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models due to an export control directive. The directive prohibited 'foreign nationals' from accessing the technology.

headline_marked: Alibaba's [[28.8M exchange Claude cloning attack]] exposed by Anthropic
headline: Alibaba's 28.8M exchange Claude cloning attack exposed by Anthropic
summary: Anthropic accuses Alibaba of massive Claude cloning attack
details: Anthropic has accused Alibaba of launching a massive attack to clone its AI model Claude. The attack involved 25,000 accounts generating over 28.8 million exchanges with Claude.

The attacks, which occurred between April 22 and June 5, targeted Claude's most valuable capabilities, such as agentic reasoning, software engineering, and long-horizon tasks. Alibaba allegedly used obfuscation techniques and proxy networks to evade detection.

Anthropic warned that without stronger interventions, these distillation attacks will help China reach advanced AI capabilities sooner. The company recommended updating antitrust laws, implementing export controls on chips, and penalizing Chinese labs for bad behavior.

The allegations come as China races to match the capabilities of Anthropic's leading model. Anthropic's letter to Senators Tim Scott and Elizabeth Warren highlighted the growing threat of AI theft and the need for stronger protections.
